# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

＃240화



노인의 칠공(七空)에서 연기가 피어올랐다.

그것은 육안으로 확인할 수 있을 만큼 밀도 높은 열양지기였고, 쉴 새 없이 노인의 작은 체구를 휘감으며 순환을 반복했다.

그리고 이내.

스아아아.

가부좌를 튼 노인의 정수리 위로 다섯 개의 고리가 차례대로 떠올랐다.

어떤 것은 푸르고 붉었으며, 어떤 것은 검고 희었다.

마지막으로 황색의 고리가 형태를 갖추자 선명한 오방색(五方色)의 고리가 완성되었다.

오기조원(五氣朝元). 모든 무림인이 원하는 꿈의 경지를 선보인 작은 체구의 노인, 적천강은 문득 눈을 떴다.

“들어오너라.”

말이 떨어지기가 무섭게 문이 열렸다.

제집인 것처럼 거침없이 안으로 들어온 넝마 차림의 청년이 주위를 둘러봤다.

“운기조식 중이신 거 아니었습니까?”

“웬 놈이 자꾸 문밖을 서성이는데 신경 쓰여서 할 수나 있겠느냐?”

“그것도 그러네요. 아, 그냥 들어와서 올림픽 구경이나 할걸.”

“올님빅인지 뭔지가 아니라 오기조원이다.”

“무슨 상관입니까. 뜻만 통하면 됐지.”

적천강은 청년, 진태경을 물끄러미 바라보았다.

“너는 어딜 다녀오는 길이냐?”

“아시잖아요. 가주이신 남궁룡 대협 뵙고 온 거.”

“남궁 가주. 그래, 그랬었지.”

낮게 뇌까리던 적천강이 물었다.

“뭐라 하더냐?”

“아, 그거요.”

진태경이 기지개를 피며 말을 이었다.

“연회 취소됐답니다.”

“연회가 취소됐다니. 그게 무슨 말이냐?”

“그게 그러니까, 창천검왕이 폐관에 들었다는데요?”

“폐관?”

“갑자기 작은 깨달음을 얻었다나 뭐라나. 여하간 그렇게 됐다네요.”

“깨달음이라…….”

적천강이 작게 고개를 끄덕였다.

“그거 공교롭구나.”

수북이 자란 턱수염을 손가락으로 배배 꼬고 있던 진태경이 멈칫했다.

“뭐가요?”

“창천검왕은 오늘을 위해 이십여 년을 기다려왔다. 한데 하필이면 오늘 그런 일이 벌어졌으니 어찌 공교롭지 않을 수 있겠느냐?”

“……막상 노야랑 붙으려고 하니까 살짝 불안했던 거 아닐까요?”

“글쎄다.”

“에이, 전 딱 알겠는데. 너무 생각이 많으신 것 아니에요?”

“그렇게 생각하느냐?”

“예. 완전.”

적천강은 세차게 고개를 끄덕이는 진태경을 말없이 응시했다.

“왜, 왜요?”

“그냥.”

“그냥이 어디 있습니까!”

“그냥 얼굴 한 번 보는 것도 네놈 허락을 맡아야 하느냐?”

“초상권, 초상권 모르세요?”

“모른다. 초상비로 머리를 밟아 주기 전에 입 다물어라.”

“옙.”

하지만 침묵은 오래가지 않았다. 진태경이 힐끔 눈치를 살피며 입을 열었기 때문이었다.

“저기, 노야.”

“왜.”

“이번 일, 잘 풀린 거 맞죠?”

“잘 풀리고 말고 할 것도 없다. 시일이 잠시 미뤄진 것일 뿐이니까.”

“그래도 시간을 벌었잖습니까.”

“노부가 질 것 같더냐?”

진태경이 황급히 손을 내저었다.

“그게 아니고요. 지금 상황으로는 이겨도 이긴 게 아니잖아요.”

이겨도 이긴 게 아니다…….

적천강은 내심 그 한마디를 중얼거렸다.

맞는 말이다. 이번 비무가 성사됐다면 승패에 상관없이 그는 큰 타격을 입었을 것이다.

창천검왕은 전력을 다해야 하는 상대.

그와의 치열한 비무에서 내상이라도 입는다면, 간신히 균형을 잡은 정기신(精氣神)이 무너질 것이다.

“노야?”

잠시 상념에 빠져 있던 적천강은 고개를 들었다. 진태경이 걱정이 담긴 눈빛으로 자신을 바라보고 있었다.

“왜 불렀느냐?”

“그냥요. 한 번 부르는 것도 허락 맡아야 합니까?”

“싱거운 놈 같으니.”

평소였다면 머리라도 한 대 쥐어박았을 텐데, 오늘만큼은 특별히 봐주기로 했다.

실소를 흘린 적천강이 자리에서 일어났다.

“가자.”

“어딜요?”

“하남.”

성라대연(星羅大宴). 지금 이 순간에도 천하 무림의 내로라하는 고수들이 속속 하남으로 집결하고 있을 것이다.

네 개의 계절을 한 바퀴 지나쳐 보낸 그들은 퍽 먼 길을 돌아온 셈이었다.

“남궁세가가 우리를 붙잡을 이유도, 우리가 남궁세가에 머무를 이유도 사라졌으니 떠나는 것이 순리다.”

“떠나는 건 좋은데, 뜨거운 물에 몸이라도 좀 불리고 가면 안 됩니까? 때가 하도 많아서 몸이 무거워요.”

“그런 말을 꺼내기에는 한참 늦었다. 요놈아. 이제 와서 깔끔한 척하지 말고, 나가서 노잣돈이라도 좀 받아 오너라. 불청객이지만 그 정도는 해 주겠지.”

“와, 이제 삥 뜯기까지 시키시네.”

“어허, 이놈이!”

“갑니다. 가요.”

투덜거리며 전각을 나서는 진태경은 알지 못했다.

적천강이 말없이 자신을 바라보고 있음을.

급하게 힘으로 오므려 채워 놓은 족쇄와 예리하게 잘려 나간 소매 끝을 바라보고 있음을.

어느새 멀어진 청년의 뒷모습을 바라보던 노인이 중얼거렸다.

“……녀석. 시키지도 않은 짓을.”

노회한 회색빛 눈동자가 저 멀리 떨어진 작은 산을 스쳤다.

푸른빛으로 뒤덮인 산등성이 위에서 옅은 먼지 구름이 흩어지고 있었다.



* * *



쾌청하던 해가 산 너머로 모습을 감추고 어둠이 내려앉았다.

나무 사이를 스치는 산바람을 맞으며 우두커니 서 있던 노인, 창천검왕 남궁천은 불쑥 입을 열었다.

“그 아이가 누구냐?”

창천검왕의 뒤에 조용히 서 있던 남궁세가의 가주, 남궁룡이 대답했다.

“산서 태원진가의 진태경이라 합니다.”

“태원진가?”

“예.”

“변방에 잠룡(潛龍)이 웅크리고 있었군.”

“바로 그 잠룡을 화왕이 품었지요.”

“틀렸다.”

창천검왕이 고개를 저었다.

“화왕은 여의주다. 화왕이 잠룡을 품은 것이 아니라, 스스로 여의주가 된 것이다.”

“……!”

남궁룡은 놀라움을 감추지 못했다. 삭막한 부자지간이라고는 하나, 그는 자신의 아버지가 어떤 사람인지 잘 알고 있었다.

말수가 적고 누군가를 평함에 있어 인색하기 그지없는 사람이라는 것도 그중 하나다.

한데 그런 분의 입에서 잠룡이라는 말이 나왔다. 천하를 떨어 울리는 화왕 적천강이 스스로 여의주가 되었다고 한다.

‘당신의 손자에게도 칭찬 한 번 없으셨던 분이…….’

섭섭함과 함께 궁금증이 일었다.

“그 정도란 말입니까?”

남궁룡의 조심스러운 물음에 창천검왕은 대답하지 않았다. 대신 느닷없는 질문을 던졌다.

Sssssss.

Some were blue and red, others black and white.

Five Qi Returning to Origin.

Jeok Cheongang, the small-framed old man who had just displayed the dream realm sought by every martial artist in Murim, suddenly opened his eyes.

“Come in.”

The door opened the moment the words left his mouth.

A young man dressed in rags strode inside as though he owned the place and looked around.

“What does it matter? As long as you got the meaning across.”

“Where have you been?”

“You know where. I went to see Great Hero Namgung Ryong, the Family Head.”

“Family Head Namgung. Right. You did.”

After muttering under his breath, Jeok Cheongang asked, “What did he say?”

“Oh, that.”

Jin Taekyung stretched before continuing.

“The banquet’s been canceled.”

“Well, apparently the Azure Sky Sword King entered seclusion.”

“Seclusion?”

“They say he suddenly gained some minor insight or something. Anyway, that’s how it turned out.”

“Enlightenment…”

Jeok Cheongang gave a small nod.

“That’s quite a coincidence.”

Jin Taekyung stopped twisting his overgrown beard around one finger.

“What is?”

“Who knows?”

“You think so?”

“Yes. Absolutely.”

“Nothing.”

“Do I need your permission just to look at your face?”

“Have you never heard of image rights?”

“No. Shut your mouth before I use Flying Over Grass[^2] to stomp on your head.”

“Who knows?”

“Come on, it’s obvious. Don’t you think you’re overthinking it?”

“You think so?”

“Yes. Absolutely.”

“W-why?”

“What?”

“Did you think this old man would lose?”

“That’s not what I meant. Given the situation, even if you won, it wouldn’t really count as a victory.”

The Azure Sky Sword King was an opponent he would have to face with everything he had.

If Jeok Cheongang suffered an Internal Injury in a fierce duel against him, the essence, qi, and spirit he had barely managed to bring into balance would collapse.

“Why did you call me?”

“What a tiresome brat.”

Normally, Jeok Cheongang would have rapped him on the head, but today, he decided to let it slide.

He let out a quiet chuckle and rose from his seat.

“Let’s go.”

“Where?”

“Henan.”

The Star-Array Grand Banquet.

Even now, the most renowned masters of Murim would be gathering in Henan one after another.

Having let all four seasons pass them by, the two of them had taken quite a detour.

“The Nangong Family has no reason to keep us here, and we have no reason to remain. Leaving is only natural.”

“Leaving sounds good, but can’t we soak in some hot water first? I’ve got so much dirt caked onto me that my body feels heavy.”

“You should have brought that up much earlier, you brat. Don’t start pretending to care about cleanliness now. Go get us some travel money. We may be uninvited guests, but they should at least give us that much.”

“Wow. Now you’re even telling me to shake people down.”

“Why, you—!”

“I’m going. I’m going.”

Jin Taekyung grumbled as he left the pavilion.

He did not know that Jeok Cheongang was silently watching him.

Watching the shackles that had been hastily forced shut by sheer strength.

Watching the cleanly severed ends of his sleeves.

The old man watched until the young man’s back had receded into the distance, then muttered,

His seasoned gray eyes swept toward a small mountain in the distance.

A faint cloud of dust was dispersing above the ridge covered in blue-green light.

The bright sun slipped behind the mountain, and darkness descended.

“His name is Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi.”

“The Jin Family of Taiyuan?”

“Yes.”

“So a Hidden Dragon was crouching in the borderlands.”

“And the Fire King took that very Hidden Dragon under his wing.”

“You’re wrong.”

The Azure Sky Sword King shook his head.

“……!”

Namgung Ryong could not hide his astonishment. Though father and son had never been close, he knew what kind of man his father was.

One of the things he knew was that his father was a man of few words who was exceedingly stingy with his judgments of others.

Yet the words *Hidden Dragon* had come from his lips.

He had even said that the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, whose name shook all under heaven, had become the dragon pearl himself.

*The man who never once praised even his own grandson…*

A pang of hurt mingled with Namgung Ryong’s curiosity.

“Is he truly that extraordinary?”

“I apologize.”

Shame filled Namgung Ryong’s reply, but the Azure Sky Sword King paid it no mind.

He had not said it to rebuke his son, who was already sixty years old.

“More than twenty years ago, when my mastery of martial arts reached eight-tenths, a question suddenly occurred to me. I wanted to test my sword.”

The clash between the Fire King and the Sword King.

The winner of that earth-shaking battle between two Supreme Peak masters had been the Fire King.

“During my secluded training, I faced countless towering walls. I struck and hammered at them without end, until at last, one of those walls collapsed.”

“Then…!”

“I have only just broken through a single wall. I have not yet achieved Great Completion.”

“Congratulations!”

Namgung Ryong performed a full bow before his father, trembling with excitement.

The Emperor’s Sword Form was the beginning and end of the dozens of secret arts possessed by the Nangong Family.

In the family’s entire history, only the founding Family Head had ever achieved Great Completion of the Emperor’s Sword Form.

True to his greatness as a martial artist, the Azure Sky Sword King had become the first in roughly a century to reach nine-tenths mastery of the Emperor’s Sword Form.

“Congratulations, is it?”

But the Azure Sky Sword King’s expression remained calm. No—he even looked hollow.

“Then let me ask you one thing. Can you withstand three moves of the Emperor’s Sword Form this old man unleashes?”

“How could I possibly dare… Surely?”

The Azure Sky Sword King quietly nodded.

Namgung Ryong’s eyes widened like lanterns.

It was unthinkable—something that neither should nor could have happened.

Yet his father had confirmed it.

That young man had withstood the Emperor’s Sword Form wielded by none other than the Azure Sky Sword King himself.

Even Namgung Ryong, who rarely lost his composure, spoke with a trembling voice.

“B-but he is only twenty-two.”

“Yes, twenty-two. He possesses the Heavenly Martial Physique and has the Fire King Jeok Cheongang as his Master.”

The Azure Sky Sword King raised his head and stared into the dark night sky.

For many long years, from the moment he first entered the world, he had lived under the name Nangong. He had carried the two characters *Azure Sky* in his heart and learned a sword that resembled the azure heavens.

But today, he had met a dragon soaring into the sky.

*I thought one move would be enough.*

He had put two-tenths of his power behind his sword, intending to teach the young man some manners.

Then three-tenths.

Then six-tenths.

And yet…

“Three moves. That’s it, right? Thanks for going easy on me.”

The young man had slung the iron balls over his shoulder and left.

All that remained in his wake were hundreds of trees and boulders carved apart by stroke after stroke, along with the mournful cries of birds that had suddenly lost their homes.

*A Hidden Dragon. A Hidden Dragon.*

The Azure Sky Sword King repeated those words in his mind, then spoke.

“Have they left?”

Namgung Ryong, who had only just gathered his wits, answered, “Yes. They left five shichen[^4] ago.”

“Where did they say they were going?”

“Henan. They said they would attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet being held there in one month.”

“The Star-Array Grand Banquet?”

The Azure Sky Sword King let out a hollow laugh.

“Make it clear to your son that he is not to show his face at this Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

* * *

Black Mountain Stronghold was a bandit organization based along one of the major routes connecting Henan and Anhui.

Its leader, Heuk Jongpil, was an illiterate former butcher, but he was also a natural-born plunderer and a master who had honed his axe techniques to the Peak realm.

Thanks to that, he commanded more than three hundred underlings and lorded over them like a king.

*Not that the Green Forest Alliance didn’t bleed me dry.*

No matter how capable Heuk Jongpil was, he was no match for the Green Forest Alliance.

The only reason he had managed to build Black Mountain Stronghold into what it was today was that he paid four-tenths of his monthly profits to the Green Forest Alliance in exchange for various forms of assistance.

For instance, the valuable intelligence delivered by the subordinate who had just entered.

“Boss, a letter arrived from the Green Forest Alliance headquarters! Here—”

Whack!

“You bastard! Don’t you know we’re all illiterate? Read it aloud!”

“It has information about the goods the Geumwa Merchant Group is transporting and the route they’re taking. They say it should arrive within two days.”

“What are you waiting for?”

“Yes?”

“Call everyone!”

The Star-Array Grand Banquet was an important event for martial artists and bandits alike.

Heuk Jongpil gathered all three hundred of his underlings and set up an ambush along the route the Geumwa Merchant Group would take.

*Just one big haul. Let us land one.*

If they managed to get their hands on even a single top-grade cat’s-eye stone, they would still have a fortune left over after paying tribute to the Green Forest Alliance.

Feeding and arming more than three hundred able-bodied men was no small task.

“They should be here by now… Why haven’t the scouts come back?”

“Who knows? We sent them out a shichen[^4] ago, but there hasn’t been any word.”

“Ugh. Trying to run a bandit operation with idiots like these is hard on the body. Hard on the body.”

The next instant, Heuk Jongpil froze mid-grumble.

With a trembling hand, he pointed toward something approaching through the darkness at incredible speed.

“……Hey. What is that?”

“I-I’m not sure either.”

Whoooosh!

Two silhouettes—one large and one small.

A long trail of red qi lingered behind them like the tail of a meteor shower.

*Are they ghosts?*

Heuk Jongpil was crouching in the grass, watching the sight, when it happened.

The two silhouettes racing along the mountain road at an unbelievable speed abruptly stopped.

A moment later, low voices drifted over.

“Why stick your nose into this?”

“It bugs me. They seem to be with those two who were skulking around earlier.”

“We’re going to be late at this rate, you brat.”

“No matter how late we are, whoever sees the trash first should clean it up.”

“Where did you learn to talk back every single time this old man says something?”

“Bastards like that always set fire to mountains.”

“You little shit! Go break all four of their limbs.”

“Yes, sir.”

Heuk Jongpil had been listening intently to their conversation.

His eyes flew wide.

“W-we’re fucking screwed! Everybody—!”

But his cry went no further.

Whoosh!

A brief rush of wind.

Then someone’s enormous hand settled companionably around his shoulder.

“Everybody, what?”

진태경이 황급히 손을 내저었다.

적천강은 내심 그 한마디를 중얼거렸다.

창천검왕은 전력을 다해야 하는 상대.

투덜거리며 전각을 나서는 진태경은 알지 못했다.

적천강이 말없이 자신을 바라보고 있음을.

급하게 힘으로 오므려 채워 놓은 족쇄와 예리하게 잘려 나간 소매 끝을 바라보고 있음을.

어느새 멀어진 청년의 뒷모습을 바라보던 노인이 중얼거렸다.

노회한 회색빛 눈동자가 저 멀리 떨어진 작은 산을 스쳤다.

푸른빛으로 뒤덮인 산등성이 위에서 옅은 먼지 구름이 흩어지고 있었다.

쾌청하던 해가 산 너머로 모습을 감추고 어둠이 내려앉았다.

나무 사이를 스치는 산바람을 맞으며 우두커니 서 있던 노인, 창천검왕 남궁천은 불쑥 입을 열었다.

“그 아이가 누구냐?”

창천검왕의 뒤에 조용히 서 있던 남궁세가의 가주, 남궁룡이 대답했다.

“산서 태원진가의 진태경이라 합니다.”

“태원진가?”

“예.”

“변방에 잠룡(潛龍)이 웅크리고 있었군.”

“바로 그 잠룡을 화왕이 품었지요.”

“틀렸다.”

창천검왕이 고개를 저었다.

“화왕은 여의주다. 화왕이 잠룡을 품은 것이 아니라, 스스로 여의주가 된 것이다.”

“……!”

남궁룡은 놀라움을 감추지 못했다. 삭막한 부자지간이라고는 하나, 그는 자신의 아버지가 어떤 사람인지 잘 알고 있었다.

말수가 적고 누군가를 평함에 있어 인색하기 그지없는 사람이라는 것도 그중 하나다.

한데 그런 분의 입에서 잠룡이라는 말이 나왔다. 천하를 떨어 울리는 화왕 적천강이 스스로 여의주가 되었다고 한다.

‘당신의 손자에게도 칭찬 한 번 없으셨던 분이…….’

섭섭함과 함께 궁금증이 일었다.

“그 정도란 말입니까?”

남궁룡의 조심스러운 물음에 창천검왕은 대답하지 않았다. 대신 느닷없는 질문을 던졌다.

“지금 네 나이 때, 이 아비는 제왕검형을 칠 성까지 익혔다. 아마 그 무렵인 듯싶구나. 천하가 나를 검왕이라 부르기 시작한 것이.”

“송구스럽습니다.”

부끄러움이 담긴 대답이었지만 창천검왕은 개의치 않았다.

이제 환갑이 된 아들을 질책하기 위해 던진 말이 아니었기 때문이다.

“이십여 년 전, 무공의 화후가 팔 성에 이르자 문득 의문이 들었다. 내 검을 시험해 보고 싶었지.”

남궁룡은 말없이 고개를 숙였다. 이후에 벌어진 일은 그도 익히 알고 있는 사실이었다.

화왕과 검왕의 격돌. 두 초절정 고수의 경천동지할 대결의 승자는 화왕이었다.

“폐관 수련을 하며 수없이 높은 벽을 마주했다. 끝없이 때리고 두드리자 마침내 벽이 무너지더구나.”

“하면……!”

“간신히 벽 하나를 넘었을 뿐, 아직 대성(大成)을 이루진 못했다.”

“감축드립니다!”

부친에게 큰절을 올리는 남궁룡은 전율했다.

제왕검형은 남궁세가에 존재하는 수십 개 절학의 시작이자 끝이다.

가문 역사상 제왕검형의 대성을 이룬 자는 초대 가주뿐.

창천검왕은 위대한 무인답게 약 백 년 만에 제왕검형의 구성(九成)에 도달한 것이다.

“감축이라.”

그러나 창천검왕의 표정은 덤덤했다. 아니, 오히려 허탈해 보이기까지 했다.

“하면 한 가지 물어보마. 너는 이 아비가 펼치는 제왕검형의 삼 초를 버틸 수 있겠느냐?”

“제가 어찌 감히…… 설마?”

조용히 고개를 끄덕이는 창천검왕을 바라보는 남궁룡의 눈이 화등잔만큼 커졌다.

있어서도 안 되고 있을 수도 없는 일.

그러나 부친이 긍정했다.

그 누구도 아닌, 창천검왕의 손에서 펼쳐진 제왕검형을 버텼노라고.

어지간해서는 평정심을 잃지 않는 남궁룡조차 목소리가 떨려 나왔다.

“하, 하지만 그의 나이는 이제 고작 스물둘에 불과합니다.”

“그래, 스물둘이지. 천무지체에 화왕 적천강을 스승으로 둔.”

오랜 세월, 그는 처음 세상에 나올 때부터 남궁의 이름으로 살아왔다. 창천이라는 두 글자를 가슴에 품었고 창천을 닮은 검을 익혔다.

‘일 초면 충분할 것이라 생각했다.’

단단히 버릇을 고쳐 줄 생각으로 이 성의 힘을 실어 검을 펼쳤다.

그다음은 삼 성이었고, 그다음은 육 성이었다.

그러나…….



‘삼 초. 끝났죠? 봐주셔서 감사합니다.’



젊은 청년은 그렇게 철구를 들쳐메고 떠났다.

‘잠룡이라. 잠룡.’

마음속으로 한 단어만 읊조리던 창천검왕이 입을 열었다.

“그들은 떠났느냐?”

가까스로 정신을 차린 남궁룡이 대답했다.

“예. 이미 다섯 시진 전에 떠났습니다.”

“어디로 간다하더냐.”

“하남입니다. 한 달 뒤 열리는 성라대연에 참석할 것이랍니다.”

창천검왕이 헛웃음을 터트렸다.

“네 아들놈에게 단단히 일러두어라. 이번 성라대연에는 이름도 내밀지 말라고.”

흑산채(黑山砦)는 하남과 안휘를 잇는 주요 길목 중 한 곳에 자리 잡은 산적 집단이었다.

빡!

“예?”

“애들 다 불러!”

삼백이 넘는 장정들을 먹이고 무장시키는 것도 여간 힘든 일이 아니다.

다음 순간, 투덜거리던 흑종필의 몸이 딱 굳었다.

“……야, 저게 뭐냐?”

“저, 저도 잘 모르겠는데요.”

쉬이이이이익!

크고 작은 두 개의 인영. 그들이 지나간 자리에는 마치 유성우의 꼬리처럼 붉은 기운으로 길게 자국이 남았다.

‘귀, 귀신인가?’

흑종필이 풀숲에 웅크려 그 광경을 지켜보던 그때였다.

믿을 수 없을 만큼 빠른 속도로 산길을 스쳐 가던 두 인영이 우뚝 멈추더니, 이내 두런거리는 말소리가 들려왔다.

“아무리 늦어도, 쓰레기는 먼저 본 사람이 치우는 게 맞습니다.”

“옙.”

두 사람의 대화에 가만히 기울이고 있던 흑종필은 눈을 번쩍 떴다.

쉬이이익!
